name: Isaac Newton Dzikum
title: Software Engineer & Computer Science Student
bio: A software engineer driven by a deep curiosity for how systems work at a foundational level. My passion lies in solving the intricate puzzles of performance, concurrency, and scalability that arise in large-scale software. I thrive on designing solutions that are not just functional, but architecturally elegant and ruthlessly efficient. My ambition is to grow into a software architect role, where I can apply these principles to build resilient, distributed systems that are built to last.

projects.title: Real-Time Typing Arena (ItchyFingers)
projects.shortDescription: An ultra-low-latency multiplayer typing platform, architected from scratch in Rust and React to support thousands of concurrent users with a seamless, real-time competitive experience.
projects.longDescription:
Architected a distributed, low-latency multiplayer platform from scratch, benchmarked to support over 10,000 concurrent WebSocket connections with sub-50ms p99 latency on Azure Container Apps.

At its core is a hybrid state management model I engineered to deliver a zero-latency feel. It combines **client-side prediction** (optimistic updates) for instant UI feedback with an adaptive, server-side input throttling system. This decouples the user's typing experience from network variability, drastically reducing server load while using a request ID (`rid`) mechanism to gracefully reconcile the client's predicted state with the server's authoritative game state.

The Rust backend is built for extreme concurrency, using a concurrent **actor model** to isolate game state and user sessions. This guarantees thread-safe state transitions and eliminates race conditions under heavy transactional load. The entire application is containerized with Docker and deployed via a zero-downtime CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions, ensuring high availability and rapid iteration.

projects.title: Rental System (Leasely)
projects.shortDescription: A multi-tenant property management system designed to streamline operations for property managers, tenants, and vendors.
projects.longDescription: Led a 5-student team to develop a full-stack tenant management system to tackle lease disputes and property mismanagement in Ghana. The system features a multi-tenant architecture with an Express.js backend using Prisma and PostgreSQL. The frontend consists of three separate, dedicated consoles for Staff, Tenants, and Vendors, all managed within a Turborepo monorepo and built with React Router v7's framework mode and Material-UI. I personally built the backend, led the team, and set up a CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions to ensure code quality and accelerate release velocity. The platform is deployed on Digital Ocean.

projects.title: Digital Chalkboard (Bloxel)
projects.shortDescription: An award-winning digital chalkboard with a realistic chalk feel, designed for low CPU usage on lecture hall systems.
projects.longDescription: Developed a high-performance digital chalkboard application with a custom algorithm for alpha compositing to simulate the layering of design chalks. The app also features algorithms for straight line correction and curve interpolation. To address system overheating in college lecture halls, I leveraged the HTML Canvas API with batch processing to offload intensive rendering computations to the GPU. The application is built with React, Tauri, and Rust, using FFI to bridge the high-performance backend with the UI.

projects.title: Cross-Platform Screen Recorder (XLab)
projects.shortDescription: A high-performance, cross-platform screen recorder built from scratch using Rust, Tauri, and FFMPEG.
projects.longDescription: Engineered a multi-threaded screen recording application from the ground up that efficiently captures, processes, and encodes frames with configurable parameters. The core logic is written in Rust for maximum performance and memory safety, with a simple React frontend presented in a Tauri window. A key feature is its efficient session management system, which handles temporary caching of frame data to the file system, ensuring constant, non-increasing memory usage during long recording sessions.

projects.title: File Explorer & Manager (Pitou)
projects.shortDescription: A feature-rich file explorer and manager for Windows, built with Tauri, Rust, and a Yew.rs frontend.
projects.longDescription: A custom file explorer desktop application designed to be fast and resource-efficient. It includes all common file operations plus advanced features like a secure folder vault, a custom recycle bin, advanced file search capabilities, file access history, and the ability to roll back actions. The entire application is built using a Rust backend with Tauri and a frontend written in Rust using the Yew.rs framework.

projects.title: Open Source Rust Libraries
projects.shortDescription: Published Rust libraries (crates) for common data structures and cryptographic operations, with thousands of downloads on crates.io.
projects.longDescription: Contributed to the open-source ecosystem by developing and publishing practical Rust libraries. This includes 'blockify', a library for essential cryptographic operations like key generation, data signing, and signature verification, and 'b_trees', a library providing efficient, AVL Tree-based data structures like ordered maps. These libraries have been downloaded thousands of times by other developers from the official Rust package registry, crates.io.
